title: Potato Waffles with Chives
changes_from_base: A savoury batter built on mashed potato and buttermilk with chives, raised with baking powder and bicarbonate and lightened with whisked whites; no sugar or vanilla.
summary: Crisp savoury waffles made from mashed potato and chives, best cooked straight away while the batter is at its lightest.
equipment: wire rack set in a baking tray

ingredients.item: riced cooked potatoes or leftover mashed potato
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Heat
steps.text: Heat the waffle iron and the oven to 93 °C with a wire rack set in a tray inside.

steps.title: Mash
steps.text: Mash and mix 319 g riced potatoes, 1 tsp salt, 2 egg yolks and 57 g butter (or 37 g oil) in a bowl until free of lumps, then beat in 450 ml buttermilk.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Whisk 180 g plain flour, 1 tsp baking powder, 1 tsp bicarbonate of soda and 3 tbsp chives in another bowl, add to the potato mixture and mix until just combined.

steps.title: Whisk
steps.text: Whisk 2 egg whites in a clean, grease-free bowl until stiff but not dry, then fold them in.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Cook the waffles straight away as the iron's instructions say, since this batter doesn't hold well, keeping finished waffles warm on the rack in the oven.

tips: Mash the potato until completely smooth and let it cool a little before adding the buttermilk, so the batter has no lumps and the waffles crisp evenly.
Use a clean, grease-free bowl for whisking the egg whites, or they won't whip up to the stiff peaks this batter needs.
Cook this batter as soon as it's mixed, since it loses its lightness if left to stand.
Keep cooked waffles on a rack rather than stacked, so steam doesn't make them soggy while the rest cook.
storage: Leftover waffles can be frozen and reheated in a toaster. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
